records.section_heading: Twenty Years of Disturbance and Change in Fagatele Bay National Marine Sanctuary, American Samoa <sup>1</sup>
records.question: Which major disturbances affected the coral reef communities in Fagatele Bay National Marine Sanctuary between 1979 and 1994?
records.ground_truth_answer: A crown-of-thorns starfish invasion in 1979, two major hurricanes (1990 and 1991), and a coral bleaching event in 1994 possibly associated with unusually high water temperatures.
ground_truth_chunks: The coral community was devastated by a crown-of-thorns starfish invasion in 1979 and has recently been affected by two major hurricanes (1990 and 1991) and a period of unusually high water temperature (1994).
An outbreak of the crown-ofthorns starfish devastated the coral communities in 1979, which led to a dramatic reduction in live coral cover in the bay (Figure 2 [Birkeland et al. 1987]).

records.question: Which coral families had mean colony size ranging from 5-20 cm?
records.ground_truth_answer: Acroporidae, Agariciidae, Faviidae, Pocilloporidae, and Poritidae.
ground_truth_chunks: Coral colony size varied among families, although no clear pattern was apparent through time (Figure 7).

In general, mean colony size ranged from small to medium (diameter = 5-20 cm) for the Acroporidae, Agariciidae, Faviidae, Pocilloporidae, and Poritidae and tended to be smaller (diameter = 1-10 cm) for the other families.

records.ground_truth_answer: Coral colony size decreased at depths of 6–9 m between 1988 and 1995.
